summary.intent: Fix CI failures on PR #501 that arose after sibling PRs #500 and #502 merged, and coordinate merging with overlapping PR #503.
summary.outcome: Three test fixes were committed (signed) and pushed to #501, and all five local checks pass outside the sandbox. GitHub CI was re-running and its result had not been seen yet.

repo: Error codes carry an implied exit code: usage-error codes map to exit 2 and all others to 1, so tests should derive the expected exit code from the error rather than hard-code 1.
Error classification (usage vs runtime) is tracked in code-classification lists: E327 is usage, while E325, E326 and E328 are runtime. #503 also adds E329 for its duplicate-package error.
#500 moved unknown config keys from a syntax-error variant to the `UnknownField` variant (E325), so tests asserting on the old variant break.
Parallel PRs (#500, #501, #502, #503) touch shared error-code and test-helper areas, so merges cause cascading test breakage and small conflicts.
Local checks need to run outside the sandbox to pass.

code.finding: Holds the error variants and code classification (usage vs runtime); the code-classification lists here will conflict between #501 and #503.
Error code documentation, modified alongside the classification changes for E325-E328.

workflow: After sibling PRs merge, re-run the full test suite on dependent PRs, since failures may stem from the merged changes rather than the PR's own diff.
When two PRs make byte-identical edits, git merges them cleanly, so conflict resolution is only needed in the divergent parts.
Verify local checks outside the sandbox and report that CI was re-triggered but not yet observed, rather than claiming success.

friction: #501's CI broke because of changes merged in #500 and #502, not its own change.
The overlap with #503 duplicates the same two test edits, guaranteeing a conflict for whichever PR merges second.
Checks needed to be run outside the sandbox to pass.
open_items: Confirm GitHub CI goes green on #501.
User needs to merge #501 and #503 (either order) and report which landed first.
Resolve the code-classification list conflict on the second PR to merge (#503 adds E329).
